patch.description: Moves a CONFIRMED one-way booking to another flight with no price difference. The body is a single `flightId`; the booking cabin, route and passenger/seat counts are kept. The replacement must be a different SCHEDULED flight on the same route, in the same cabin and on the same airline, with enough available seats; the booked flight must not have departed. The booking total is recomputed from the stored passenger counts and the stored segment baggage fee (kept as is, never repriced on the replacement) plus the replacement cabin fare. Only an unchanged total is accepted: a higher or lower fare answers 409 with the difference and changes nothing, because charging/refunding a difference needs a Payments-owned contract that is documented but not implemented yet. In one MongoDB transaction the replacement is re-read with the transaction session and must still be SCHEDULED and before departure (so a flight cancelled after the first check cannot receive the booking), the replacement cabin gets the booked seats using the same atomic availability guard as a hold, the booking is updated only while it is still CONFIRMED on the old flight, and the old booked seats are returned. A failed change or a concurrent winner rolls the whole transaction back, so old seats are never released on failure and are never released twice. The booking id, unique booking reference, passengers, payment reference and CONFIRMED status are preserved; no second booking, payment or refund is created. Round-trip bookings answer 409 until the product rule for them is agreed. Another traveler and an unknown id both answer 404; only role USER can call it.

post.description: Two steps on the same owner-only endpoint. First send `{ confirm: false }`: it validates ownership and eligibility, computes the refund from the outbound segment's airline cancellation tiers (Payments' RefundCalculator, full booking total, fractional days before departure) and returns the amount, currency and applied tier without changing anything. Then send `{ confirm: true, expectedRefundAmountCents: <the previewed amount> }`: the amount is recomputed and must still match, otherwise the request answers 409 with the current amount and nothing is cancelled or refunded (a fresh preview and confirmation are required). `confirm` is required and must be a boolean; a missing value is a validation error, never consent. On a match the confirmed amount is recorded on the booking (only while it is still CONFIRMED), then the booking goes through BookingLifecycle to CANCELLED, every segment's booked seats return to inventory in the same transaction, and the positive recorded refund is issued through PAY-03's RefundsService.issue. A zero refund (no applicable tier or a 0% tier) is recorded as 0, cancels and releases the seats without calling issue and returns `refund: null`. If issuing the refund fails after the cancellation (for example the payment provider is unavailable), the answer is 503 and the booking stays CANCELLED with its recorded amount. Sending the same confirmation again completes the refund with exactly the amount recorded at the first cancellation (no tier is re-read, the departure is not rechecked) and answers 200; it never returns the seats twice. A further retry after the refund was issued, a legacy cancellation with no recorded amount, or a cancellation that had nothing to refund answers 409. Only a CONFIRMED booking may be cancelled and only before the outbound departure; a round trip is cancelled as a whole using the outbound segment's airline and tier. Another traveler and an unknown id answer 404. A preview of a cancelled booking answers 409.
